experiments.scope: Reduced event on the selected Orchard Poseidon target at its own round count: the first 14 bits of the big-endian reading of the 32-byte digest agree for two distinct canonical messages. One birthday search per organizer trial over fresh inputs from the trial seed. No full collision is expected or claimed.
experiments.hypothesis: A search of at most 1200 fresh inputs returns a pair whose digests agree on those 14 bits in every trial, as a random 14-bit function would. Checks the digest of the selected target at one reduced width; it says nothing about the full-width map, the cost or the success probability.

experiments.scope: Reduced event on the selected Orchard Poseidon target at its own round count, on the line construction of proof.md section 2: the first 6 bits of the big-endian reading of the 32-byte digest agree for two distinct canonical messages that are the antipodal points W = c+s and W = c-s about a centre c of the line j = 0 of the first two rounds. One scan of the pairs s = 1, ..., 150 per organizer trial, the centre from the trial seed. No full collision is expected or claimed.
experiments.hypothesis: The digest difference F(c+s) - F(c-s) = 2 s g_c(s^2) of the antipodal points behaves as a random function of s at width 6: a trial returns a pair with probability 1-(1-2^-6)^150 = 0.9058, about 232 of the 256 trials. Checks the digest of the selected target on the antipodal line pairs of the construction at one reduced width; it says nothing about the full-width map, the cost or the success probability.

experiments.scope: Euclidean normality of the algorithm's own construction at reduced depth, on the selected Orchard Poseidon target (proof.md 9.5, 10.5.1). Two centres per trial, the first from the trial seed, the second from the seed and its index. For each centre c the program builds F_2(c + X), the coordinate 0 after the first 2 S-box layers on the line j = 0 of the first two rounds (the F_N of proof.md 10.3, degree 25), its monic odd part g about c (degree m = 12), R = X^((p-1)/2) mod g and the complete Euclidean remainder sequence of (g, R - 1), exactly over F_p. All 256 trials are computed, 512 sequences. A trial whose two sequences are both normal (deg(R - 1) = m - 1 and every quotient of degree 1 down to the gcd) and pass the self-checks returns two distinct canonical messages on the line whose digests agree on the first 6 bits, found among 65 line points (certain, by pigeonhole); any other trial returns two nulls. The final letter of the id only changes the organizer seeds. No full collision is expected or claimed.
experiments.hypothesis: Every computed sequence is normal, so exactly 256 of the 256 trials return a pair and the abnormal count is zero in 512 sequences. Per trial the program reports the untrusted observations sequences, normal_sequences, selfcheck_ok, abnormal_quotients, gcd_positive and max_quotient_degree. The sequences of all euclid-normal experiments are independent draws of the centre, so zero abnormal sequences in N of them bound the abnormality at m = 12 by 3/N (rule of three, one-sided 95%). Supports the premise H-NORMAL of proof.md 9.5 at m = 12 on the construction's own pairs; it says nothing about the scale m of the claim, the cost or the success probability.
